title: Montélimar nougat
subtitle: French white nougat with pistachios and almonds
excerpt: Montélimar nougat is a firm, chewy white confection from the Drôme valley, made by cooking sugar and honey to hard-crack stage and folding the hot syrup into stiff beaten egg whites. It sets with whole toasted almonds and pistachios suspended through it, slicing into neat, slightly sticky bars. The texture is dense and pulls like firm taffy, not the soft Italian version.
sourceNotes: Nougat de Montélimar has protected geographical indication (IGI) status in France. French law defines it as containing at least 30% almonds and 28% honey by weight, set in a firm, light-coloured mass. The town of Montélimar in the Drôme has made nougat since at least the 17th century, when abundant lavender honey and locally grown almonds combined with sugar from the southern trade routes. The home recipe here doesn't carry the IGI designation but follows the traditional technique: cooking sugar and glucose to hard-crack stage (145,150°C) and honey to a separate high temperature, beating both into egg whites in sequence.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps in an airtight container, layers separated by rice paper, for up to 6 weeks.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make at least 8 hours ahead; the nougat needs overnight to firm properly before cutting.
recipe.temperatureNote: hard-crack stage; requires two thermometer readings simultaneously

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: hard-crack stage for the sugar syrup (145–150°C); honey is cooked separately to 130°C; both require precise thermometer readings

content.text: Montélimar nougat is a firm, chewy white sweet made by cooking sugar to hard-crack stage and folding it into stiff egg whites. It sets to a dense, slightly stretchy bar packed with toasted nuts. This is advanced confectionery: you are managing two syrups simultaneously, both at temperatures above 130°C, while keeping the mixer running. If hot syrup touches skin, run cold water over it for at least ten minutes and seek medical care if needed. Read the method all the way through before you start.
Toast the nuts and prepare the tin

Preheat the oven to 160°C. Spread the almonds on a tray and roast for 10 minutes until pale gold. Add the pistachios for the final 3 minutes. Remove and keep them warm in the turned-off oven, cold nuts will deflate the nougat when folded in. Line a 20 cm square tin with two sheets of rice paper, one on the base and one set aside for the top.

Start both syrups at the same time. In a medium saucepan combine the sugar, glucose syrup, and water. In a small saucepan heat the honey. Clip a probe thermometer to each pan. Cook both over a medium heat, without stirring after they begin to bubble. The honey is ready first at 130°C; the sugar syrup follows at 145,150°C. Monitor both at once and have the stand mixer ready.
Beat the whites, pour in the syrups

When the honey reaches 130°C, start beating the egg whites in the stand mixer on medium-high speed until they form stiff peaks. Pour the honey in a thin, steady stream down the inside of the bowl with the mixer running. Do not pour it onto the whisk. Increase to high speed and beat for 2 minutes. When the sugar syrup reaches 145,150°C, pour it in the same way, thin stream, down the side, mixer running. Add the vanilla. Beat on high for 5 minutes; the mixture will be very stiff and glossy.
Fold in nuts and set overnight

Working quickly, fold in the warm nuts with a lightly oiled spatula. The mixture stiffens fast as it cools. Tip into the lined tin, smooth the top with oiled parchment, and press the second sheet of rice paper over the surface. Leave at room temperature overnight, at least 8 hours. Cut into bars or squares with a lightly oiled sharp knife. Wrap each piece in cellophane or parchment to prevent sticking.
